items.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 6 at 2:20AM PDT until October 8 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures ranging
from the mid 80s to lower 90s at the beaches to the mid 90s to
around 100 for the mesas and other higher coastal terrain. Nights
will be very warm with low temperatures in the upper 60s to mid
70s.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
items.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

items.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 6 at 1:27AM PDT until October 9 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from this afternoon
through Friday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6
AM Wednesday to 11 AM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Minor coastal erosion is also
expected. Additionally, elevated surf will lead to strong rip
currents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated surf of 3-5 feet, with sets to 6
feet, on south- and southwest-facing beaches. High tides are
expected to peak between 6.5 and 7.0 feet during the mornings
and evenings.
items.instruction:
A beach hazards statement for elevated surf means that waves will
be high enough to cause danger to inexperienced swimmers in the
water. Elevated surf also frequently results in strong rip
currents which can drag people away from the shore and possibly
result in drowning. Always swim near a lifeguard.

A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that tides and elevated surf
will combine to generate localized flooding of low areas along the
shore.
